question: Acceptance testing an outdoor disconnect with no interrupter attachment, you find the key interlock lets it open while the feeding breaker is still closed. The contractor says that’s fine if the switch is opened briskly. What is your call?
choices: Accept it; opening the blade fast lets it break load current, so leave it as is
Write it up and fix the interlock before energizing; no interrupting rating
Accept it as long as the switch has a grounding blade
Accept it, but tell operators to stop the blade partway if it arcs
explanation: A disconnect without an interrupter has no interrupting rating. It may break only small currents such as line charging or magnetizing current, and even that draws an open arc. The interlock is what keeps load off the switch when someone operates it, so ATS has you prove its sequencing. Fast operation cuts arcing time in normal switching but doesn’t make it a load-break device. If a switch is still arcing at about two-thirds of blade travel, C37.30.1 says reclose it if practical, not stop it.

question: On a three-pole gang-operated open air switch, the handle and indicator show closed. Contact resistance across the A and C blades is similar, but B reads more than double the lowest, and there is no manufacturer data. What is the right next step?
choices: Accept it; the position indicator proves all three blades closed
Re-torque the terminal pads and retest; blade contact cannot be what caused this high reading
Check B for full closure, penetration, alignment, and latching; adjust the linkage and retest
Run a dielectric withstand test on B to check the insulators
explanation: Without manufacturer data, ATS has you investigate a blade reading more than 50 percent above the lowest similar pole, and B is well past that. On a gang-operated switch, a bent pipe or slipped linkage can leave one blade short of full travel while the handle reads closed. C37.30.1 wants each blade looked at after operation and all blades checked for closing together and seating. Fix the mechanical cause, then retest contact resistance.
reference: ANSI/NETA ATS-2025 7.5.1.3.A.7, B.2, and D.2; MTS-2023 7.5.1.3.A.5 and D.2; ref. IEEE C37.30.1-2022, D.3.2.1 item b) and D.4 item g)

question: Maintaining a de-energized, grounded open air switch, you find light pitting on the main contacts, an arcing horn with heavy burn damage, and a blade latch that doesn’t hold firmly. Which plan fits?
choices: Dress the light pitting on an emery wheel, leave the horn with the heavy burn damage where it is, and grease the latch that does not hold firmly
Replace the whole switch, since any pitting means end of life
Leave it all; pitting and horn damage don’t matter on a disconnect
Dress light pitting with fine sandpaper (not emery) or as the maker says; replace the horn; set latch, alignment, and pressure; retest
explanation: Light pitting can be dressed, but heavily eroded parts and arc-damaged horns get replaced, and emery is off the table. The latch adjustment, alignment, and contact pressure are all on the maintenance checklist before the switch goes back. Finish with a contact-resistance test across each blade and compare the poles.
reference: ANSI/NETA MTS-2023 7.5.1.3.A.5 and B.2; ref. IEEE C37.30.1-2022, D.4 items b), d), and e)

question: An outdoor group-operated air switch on a 14.4 kV system gets a dielectric withstand test, and the manufacturer is silent. ATS 7.5.1.3 sends you to Table 100.19, which gives a maximum ac test voltage of:
choices: 27 kV
explanation: Table 100.19 lists 20.4 kV ac and 28.8 kV dc for the 14.4 kV class. The 15.6 kV value belongs to the 8.3 kV class, and 27 kV is a switchgear value from Table 100.2. Source: ANSI/NETA ATS-2025 7.5.1.3.B.5 and Table 100.19.

question: Which inspection item is in ATS 7.5.1.3 for a motor-operated open air switch but not in the low-voltage switch procedure?
choices: Blade alignment and travel stops
Fuse size against the coordination study
Grounding of the enclosure
Motor-operator limit switch adjustment
explanation: Open medium- and high-voltage air switches often have a motor operator, so ATS checks its limit switches and mechanical interlocks. ATS 7.5.1.3 also has you record the operation counter. Source: ANSI/NETA ATS-2025 7.5.1.3.A.6.
